chunks: From him, from Mūsā ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn Hilāl, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jaʿfar ibn ʿUthmān, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام regarding Maghrib: At times we pray while fearing that the sun may still be behind the mountain, while the mountain has screened it from us.
He said: It is not upon you to climb the mountain.

So there is no contradiction between these two reports and what we have considered regarding the disappearance of the sun, namely the vanishing of the redness from the eastern side; for it is not impossible that the redness has vanished from it even though the sun still remains behind the mountain, because it sets for some people and rises for others.

He only forbade pursuing it and climbing the mountain to see it because that is not obligatory. Rather, what is obligatory upon him is to observe his east and west together with the removal of confusion and excuses. The second way of understanding the reports we presented is that they are specific to one who has excuses and one who has a necessary need; this indicates that.

key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, whose disappearance marks the entry of Maghrib
key_terms.اللُّبْسِ: confusion or uncertainty regarding the time
key_terms.الْجَبَلِ: the mountain that may obstruct direct sight of the sun
key_terms.الْحُمْرَةِ: the redness/twilight glow used here as a sign related to sunset
key_terms.الْمَشْرِقِ: the eastern side, from which the redness is observed to vanish
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the time of Maghrib salat (prayer), beginning after sunset
key_terms.غَيْبُوبَةِ: the disappearance or setting from sight

ai.seo_question: Is it necessary to climb a mountain to confirm sunset before performing Maghrib salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This report concerns the time of Maghrib salat (prayer) and explains that one is not required to climb a mountain to verify the sun’s setting. It reconciles reports by treating the disappearance of eastern redness as the operative sign, while also noting that some narrations may apply specifically to those with excuses or pressing need.
